strings.d1.s0.name: Railay West Beach
strings.d1.s0.tips: 15 minutes by longtail boat from Ao Nang (100 THB). A beach between limestone cliffs, quiet in the morning and a hub for rock climbing.
strings.d1.s1.name: Phra Nang Cave Beach
strings.d1.s1.tips: In the rainy season the morning can be sunny, but expect waves.
strings.d1.s2.name: Railay Viewpoint & Lagoon
strings.d1.s2.tips: A red-earth rope climb (short but steep) leads to the view. Going down to the lagoon takes nerve.
strings.d1.s3.name: Mangrove Restaurant Railay East
strings.d1.s3.tips: Thai food by the mangroves; try the green curry.
strings.d1.s4.name: Ao Nang Sunset Wang Sai
strings.d1.s4.tips: Seafood at the far end of Ao Nang. Watch the sunset, then take the 17:30 longtail back.
strings.d1.b0.name: Tonsai Beach
strings.d1.b0.tips: A hippie climbers' beach. Walk there at low tide; choose it for the scenery.
strings.d1.b1.name: Krua Thara Seafood Klong Muang
strings.d1.b1.tips: A local seafood favourite in Klong Muang.
strings.d2.s0.name: Four Islands Tour Ao Nang
strings.d2.s0.tips: Longtail (1,000) or speedboat (1,500); the national park fee of 400 is extra.
strings.d2.s1.name: Koh Poda
strings.d2.s1.tips: White sand and a towering rock. Snorkel here; it is Ao Nang's postcard view.
strings.d2.s2.name: Chicken Island Koh Gai
strings.d2.s2.tips: A rock shaped like a chicken's head; snorkel among the fish.
strings.d2.s3.name: Koh Tup Sandbar Lunch
strings.d2.s3.tips: At low tide a sandbar (Talay Waek) joins three islands. Lunch with rice is included.
strings.d2.s4.name: Phra Nang Cave Beach & Return
strings.d2.s4.tips: The last stop is Phra Nang; you are back in Ao Nang at 16:00.
strings.d2.b0.name: Hong Island Tour
strings.d2.b0.tips: Hong's lagoon and 360° views, as an alternative to the Four Islands (unless you are going the next day).
strings.d2.b1.name: Ao Nang Night Market
strings.d2.b1.tips: A night market from Friday to Sunday; try pad thai and mango sticky rice.
strings.d3.s0.name: Hong Island Speedboat
strings.d3.s0.tips: 30 minutes from Ao Nang, in Than Bok Khorani National Park.
strings.d3.s1.name: Hong Lagoon
strings.d3.s1.tips: A hidden lagoon ringed by cliffs; go by kayak.
strings.d3.s2.name: Koh Hong Main Beach
strings.d3.s2.tips: White sand and coral, plus a 360° viewing platform (419 steps, new in 2019).
strings.d3.s3.name: Koh Hong Picnic Lunch
strings.d3.s3.tips: Included in the tour; eaten on the beach.
strings.d3.s4.name: Koh Lao Lading & Pakbia
strings.d3.s4.tips: A small cove on Paradise Island; snorkel, then head back at 16:00.
strings.d3.b0.name: Krabi Town Chao Fah Night Market
strings.d3.b0.tips: Riverside evening food stalls in Krabi Town.
strings.d3.b1.name: Tup Kaek Beach
strings.d3.b1.tips: If you skip the tour: a quiet beach north of Ao Nang, good for sunset.
strings.d4.s0.name: Tiger Cave Temple Wat Tham Suea
strings.d4.s0.tips: 1,260 steps (steep!) to a summit Buddha and 360° panorama. Go at 07:00 when it is cool; watch for monkeys and bring water.
strings.d4.s1.name: Krabi Town Breakfast Ruen Mai
strings.d4.s1.tips: A garden restaurant serving Thai and southern dishes.
strings.d4.s2.name: Emerald Pool Sa Morakot
strings.d4.s2.tips: An emerald-green natural pool in the forest (1 km wooden walkway) in Khao Phra Bang Khram, 1 hour by car.
strings.d4.s3.name: Blue Pool
strings.d4.s3.tips: A blue spring where swimming is banned, 800 m beyond the Emerald Pool.
strings.d4.s4.name: Klong Thom Hot Springs
strings.d4.s4.tips: Hot spring pools at 40°C in a forest stream, with a waterfall.
strings.d4.b0.name: Khao Khanab Nam Caves
strings.d4.b0.tips: Longtail from Krabi Town; caves and mangroves between two rock hills, instead of the pools.
strings.d4.b1.name: Ko Klang Village Lunch
strings.d4.b1.tips: Home cooking in a Muslim fishing village; arrive by boat.
strings.d5.s0.name: Phi Phi Speedboat Ao Nang
strings.d5.s0.tips: 45 minutes by speedboat (tour about 2,500 THB); the national park fee is 400.
strings.d5.s1.name: Maya Bay
strings.d5.s1.tips: The bay from the film The Beach. Access has been restricted since 2022 (no walking on the beach, no swimming). It is empty at 08:00-09:00 and CLOSED in August and September.
strings.d5.s2.name: Pileh Lagoon & Viking Cave
strings.d5.s2.tips: Swim in the emerald lagoon; see the swiftlet nest cave from outside.
strings.d5.s3.name: Phi Phi Don Tonsai Lunch
strings.d5.s3.tips: Buffet included in the tour, in the island village.
strings.d5.s4.name: Bamboo Island
strings.d5.s4.tips: White sand and snorkelling; head back at 16:30.
strings.d5.b0.name: Phi Phi Viewpoint
strings.d5.b0.tips: The classic view over two bays, a 20-minute climb. Do it instead of Bamboo.
strings.d5.b1.name: Ao Nang Krua Thara Dinner
strings.d6.s0.name: Klong Muang Beach
strings.d6.s0.tips: Ao Nang's quiet neighbour; a resort beach for swimming.
strings.d6.s1.name: Tub Kaek Beach
strings.d6.s1.tips: An empty beach with views of the Hong islands, and the start of the Dragon Crest (Khao Ngon Nak) trail.
strings.d6.s2.name: Lae Lay Grill
strings.d6.s2.tips: A well-known hilltop Thai restaurant with sea views, in Ao Nang.
strings.d6.s3.name: Thai Cooking Class Ya's Krabi
strings.d6.s3.tips: A half-day cooking course with a market visit and 5 dishes.
strings.d6.b0.name: Khao Ngon Nak Dragon Crest
strings.d6.b0.tips: A 3.7 km forest climb with cliff-top rock views, instead of the beach.
strings.d6.b1.name: Jenna's Bistro Ao Nang
strings.d6.b1.tips: Thai and Western food; an evening option instead of the course.
strings.d7.theme: Ao Nang morning and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Ao Nang Beach Morning Walk
strings.d7.s0.tips: Morning longtails on the sand; the Monkey Trail leads to Pai Plong beach.
strings.d7.s1.name: Pai Plong Beach
strings.d7.s1.tips: A cove by the Centara resort; snorkel and look out for monkeys.
strings.d7.s2.name: Café 8.98 Ao Nang
strings.d7.s2.tips: Breakfast and coffee for your farewell.
strings.d7.s3.name: Krabi Airport Minibus
strings.d7.s3.tips: 40 minutes from Ao Nang; time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Ao Nang Landmark Night Market Morning
strings.d7.b0.tips: For souvenirs, instead of the beach.
strings.d7.b1.name: Ao Nang Roti Stand
strings.note0: Stay in Ao Nang (Railay is pricey, Krabi Town is quiet). The Railay longtail costs 100 THB; use Grab or a scooter. The airport minibus is 150.
strings.note1: November to April is the dry season: 30°C and glassy seas (the best time). December to February is crowded and expensive, and April brings Songkran.
strings.note2: Fill in the TDAC digital arrival card; carry cash in THB. Island tours cost 1,000-2,500 plus a 400 park fee; a taverna meal is 200-400; round up your tips.
strings.note3: Do Tiger Cave at 07:00 (heat and monkeys), take the 08:00 slot at Maya Bay, and expect the Four Islands to be crowded at midday. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and water shoes.
strings.note4: You will get wet on the morning longtail (bring a dry bag); there are few ATMs in Railay.
strings.note5: Southern Thai food: massaman, gaeng som (sour curry), roti and coconut seafood. Muslim villages serve halal food.
